transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-01-05 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~55 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Novum Head of Security), Tomislav K (Platform), Aisha Khan (Compliance), Ben Yoon (SRE)

Summary: quick intake to understand Novum Ledger's data residency and audit evidence needs. Primary constraints: EU customer data footprint, financial transaction PII, PCI-adjacent concerns, and strict log retention/minimization. Team exploring Hosted for speed vs Dedicated/Private for strict control.

Topics: GDPR residency, log redaction/minimization, keystore (KMS) residency and HSM/escrow questions, SOC2 / audit evidence flow, SSO/SAML and RBAC, network isolation (VPC vs private on-prem), chain-of-custody for logs, sample retention windows and legal hold processes.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for taking time. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Priya: Priya here, head of security at Novum.
[00:08] Tom: Tomislav, platform lead.
[00:10] Aisha: Aisha from compliance.
[00:12] Ben: Ben, SRE.
[00:15] Maya: Great, I'll hand to Diego for a short tech overview of how Redwood surfaces hosting options, then we'll dig into your constraints.
[00:22] Diego: Cool, thanks. So at a high level Redwood offers Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC or on-prem) — common knobset is placement of keys and logs. For Hosted we operate the control plane, but you can opt for customer-managed KMS with some caveats; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and better network segmentation; Private is full control, either in your VPC or on-prem boxed.
[00:45] Priya: When you say customer-managed KMS for Hosted, do keys ever transit Redwood infrastructure? We need proof that keys never leave EU boundaries for certain data classes.
[00:54] Diego: Good question. For Hosted with customer-managed KMS, the key material is in the customer KMS. However ephemeral session keys are negotiated — I know that sounds fuzzy. We have customers where the KMS is region-locked to eu-west-1 and we provide audit trails showing key usage logs. We can pull those and include in evidence packs.
[01:12] Aisha: Audit packs are important. We need a reproducible chain-of-custody for model calls touching regulated data — who, when, what model version, and log linkage to request IDs.
[01:22] Maya: Totally, and Redwood Console exposes per-request traces and token-level cost/latency breakdowns. We also store model version, route, and request id. For Private deploys this is all in your control but we can ship the control-plane artifacts for audits.
[01:35] Tom: Are those logs ever aggregated with other tenants in Hosted? Our legal team will not accept co-mingling of audit logs for EU regulated flows.
[01:42] Diego: In standard Hosted, operational logs are multi-tenant but customer request traces and content logs are separated. That said many customers requiring strict non-co-mingling choose Dedicated with tenancy isolation or Private.
[01:55] Ben: What's the retention window flexibility? We have a policy: minimal retention on raw request text, 30 days for derived telemetry, and 7 years for aggregated billing.
[02:05] Aisha: Plus we need legal hold capabilities — if there is a regulatory subpoena, retention gets extended.
[02:09] Diego: We can configure retention per workspace for Dedicated/Private. Hosted has standard retention but we support retention exceptions with enterprise contracts; legal hold can be captured in our audit logging but you'll need a contract clause.
[02:25] Priya: For GDPR we also need data subject access ability — deletion vs redaction. How does Redwood handle deletion of cached prompts or KV cache?
[02:35] Diego: Good call — KV cache and prefix caches can be flushed per-tenant. In Hosted automatic prefix caching is on by default for throughput efficiency but we can disable caching for regulated routes or set TTLs; for Dedicated/Private you control cache policies fully.
[02:52] Maya: Quick clarification: when you say 'flush' is that immediate? We need a demonstrable action in the audit log showing the cache flush event.
[03:00] Diego: Yes, flush events are recorded with timestamps and operator ID for Dedicated/Private; for Hosted we produce an event and it goes through the control plane — sometimes the operator is a Redwood service account which we include in the evidence bundle. We realize customers often want customer-controlled operators, which is why Private is often chosen.
[03:18] Tom: We're also doing cross-border payments; some metadata is allowed to leave EU in pseudonymized form, but transaction payloads must stay in EU. Can Redwood route only particular routes to EU-hosted models?
[03:30] Maya: Yes, routing policies are supported. You can pin routes to region or model variant. We can set policy to always route 'payments' workspace to eu regions and fallback to other models only if needed, with an alert.
[03:41] Priya: How are fallbacks logged? If a fallback triggers to an offshore model, we need automatic email to compliance and an incident log.
[03:49] Diego: Fallbacks generate a trace entry and we can wire an alert to your Slack or PagerDuty. By default the trace includes the reason for fallback and the selected variant; we can also add a policy to fail closed instead of fallback.
[04:05] Ben: Latency concerns — if we go region-restricted to eu-west-1 and run larger models, do you support dedicated GPUs in region?
[04:14] Diego: Yes, Dedicated can be region-specific. For Private on-prem you bring hardware. Our recommendation: for strict residency + p95 latency targets, Dedicated in-region is typical.
[04:26] Aisha: On encryption: we need guarantees of at-rest encryption with customer keys and HSM-backed keystore for certain data classes. Does Redwood support HSM-backed KMS or key escrow?
[04:38] Diego: We support customer-provided HSM-backed KMS (e.g., cloud KMS with HSM). For Private installs you can plug in your HSM. Key escrow is possible for very large enterprise deals, we have a process but it's not standard — requires legal/ops integration.
[04:55] Maya: Priya, do you have a prioritized list of controls? It might help us map quickly to Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
[05:03] Priya: Yes — 1) EU-only residency for transaction payloads, 2) No log co-mingling, 3) Customer-managed keys (HSM ideal), 4) Legal hold & retention override, 5) Per-request trace and immutable chain-of-custody. If those fail then we need Private.
[05:22] Diego: Understood. We can probably meet 1-4 in Dedicated with the right contract addenda. For 5, Private gives the clearest chain-of-custody but Dedicated with isolated logging and signed evidence packs can usually suffice for SOC2 audits.
[05:40] Tom: What does an evidence pack look like? Is it human readable? Machine readable? Can auditors query it?
[05:46] Maya: The evidence pack is a zipped bundle — logs, trace ids, model version manifest, KMS usage logs, and signed statements. For Hosted we provide it via secure link to your compliance team. For Dedicated/Private we can provide direct access. It is mostly machine-readable JSON with human-friendly index files.
[06:02] Aisha: For data deletion requests (DSAR) we need proof that content was removed, including any backups. Backups are a big sticking point.
[06:11] Diego: Backups for Hosted are handled by Redwood ops with region locking; we can provide backup manifests and deletion timestamps. For Dedicated/Private, backups are managed by your infra team (or ours if you contract it) and you can implement your own backup deletion processes.
[06:26] Priya: One more: is there a way to pseudo-anonymize payloads before they hit the model in Hosted? We prefer to scrub PII client-side if possible.
[06:34] Diego: You can deploy a pre-processing layer in front of our API — we have customers who run a scrubber as a sidecar or Lambda to remove PII and pass only tokens. Redwood also supports function/tool calling so you can pipe sanitized content.
[06:46] Ben: If we do pre-scrubbing, how do we prove to auditors that original data wasn't captured somewhere?
[06:52] Maya: That's where client-side processing + signed attestations come in — you can keep a truncated ingest hash only and provide that as evidence. We'll help design that flow.
[07:01] Tom: About pricing: what's the delta if we choose Dedicated in eu-west-1 vs Hosted ephemeral? Our finance team will want ballpark.%
[07:10] Maya: We'll follow up with a pricing sheet. High level: Dedicated has a fixed monthly reservation plus lower per-token pricing; Hosted is pure usage but higher per-token. Private adds platform licensing and ops. We'll send numbers after this call.
[07:24] Priya: For HIPAA — we have a small dataset used for customer support that is PHI-adjacent. Is Redwood willing to sign BAA for Hosted?
[07:34] Diego: We sign BAAs for certain enterprise plans; Hosted BAAs often require specific controls and account provisioning. Many health customers choose Dedicated or Private for extra control.
[07:47] Aisha: Can you walk through an incident where a fallback mistakenly routed to non-EU and what the evidence artifact looked like?
[07:55] Diego: I can summarize a redacted example: fallback occurred during a transient capacity event; we had an automated policy that allowed failover to a US region. Post-incident we provided a timeline, traces, request ids, the fallback reason, and confirmation that content wasn't persisted in the fallback region beyond ephemeral caches; we also provided proof of cache purge. That incident pushed the customer to change policy to fail closed.
[08:24] Priya: That kind of historical artifact is exactly what we'll need pre-procurement.
[08:28] Maya: Noted. We'll include a redacted incident binder in the follow-up.
[08:35] Tom: Operational question — RBAC and SSO. We use SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning. Can you map Redwood roles to our internal groups and limit access to logs?
[08:44] Diego: Yes, we support SAML 2.0 and SCIM. RBAC supports workspace-level roles and fine-grained log access can be gated by role. For Hosted, audit trails show which Redwood admin accessed certain artifacts; Dedicated and Private give you full control of access policies.
[09:02] Ben: Any gotchas with VPC peering and egress flows? We need to ensure no unexpected egress to public IPs for certain subnets.
[09:10] Diego: VPC peering is supported for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we offer private connectivity options via partner connectivity; egress rules can be locked down in Private.
[09:20] Aisha: One compliance nuance — our legal team wants assurance that any third-party sub processors used by Redwood maintain equivalent controls and are documented.
[09:29] Maya: We'll provide our subprocessor registry and SOC2 scope docs. We also include third-party attestations in the evidence bundle.
[09:38] Priya: When can we run a pilot? We want to validate latency and confirm traceability.
[09:42] Maya: Timeline depends on contract. For a light pilot (non-production) we can spin up a Dedicated staging pool within ~2 weeks if capacity available; otherwise a Hosted pilot starts immediately with some enterprise guardrails.
[09:55] Tom: If we do Dedicated staging, can we get a small reserved node in eu-west-1 for two weeks for benchmarking?
[10:01] Diego: Yes, Diego: that's doable, I'll scope.
[10:04] Maya: Cool. Let's summarize next steps.
[10:07] Maya: Action items recap: Diego will draft a basic benchmark plan and small staging topology; Maya will send SOC2 + subprocessor list + redacted incident binder; Priya will share retention & DSAR templates; Novum to confirm pilot dates.
[10:20] Priya: Sounds good. Any blockers we should flag?
[10:23] Aisha: Legal wants clear backup deletion proof — that's the big one.
[10:27] Maya: Understood. We'll include backup manifests in the evidence pack and outline deletion flows.
[10:32] Ben: One last nit: can we get a short architecture note for the pre-scrubbing pattern you mentioned?
[10:36] Diego: I'll include a 1-page pattern doc with sequence diagrams.
[10:40] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up via email, I'll attach the items and propose pilot windows.
[10:45] Tom: Thanks.
[10:47] Priya: Thanks all.

End of transcript.

References mentioned: SOC2 report, subprocessor registry (link to be provided), redacted incident binder (will be sent), privacy/data-retention templates, benchmarking plan spreadsheet.
